ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all natural persons and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the South African domestic targeted financial sanctions list maintained by the National Treasury; enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs) in accordance with FICA; continuous transaction monitoring, risk rating, and five-year record keeping obligations apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Online Transaction System (www.cipc.co.za / eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed company name may be in any of South Africa's eleven official languages and must end with 'Proprietary Limited' or the abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'. Non-Latin or diacritic characters require a Latin-alphabet transliteration; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, trademark, or close corporation name, and must comply with the Companies Act 71 of 2008 naming restrictions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection CIPC issues a notice stating the statutory grounds. The applicant may request written reasons and file an application for reconsideration with CIPC within 20 business days of rejection; failing that, a formal appeal may be lodged with the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. The appeal must be filed with the Registrar of the Companies Tribunal and served on the Commissioner of CIPC, after which the Tribunal must adjudicate within the prescribed statutory timeframe.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual or mail-forwarding address is not permissible. The registered office must be a physical street address in South Africa at which legal process may be served. A serviced or co-working office with dedicated facilities, staffed during business hours and capable of receiving service, may qualify as a permissible 'virtual office' for this industry, provided the company's statutory records are available for inspection at that address. For ISIC 5222 marine bunkering operations, regulatory authorities will expect demonstrable commercial substance beyond a nominal registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high: approximately 35% annualised probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first three years, driven by the medium-risk AML/CFT classification and the statutory licensing requirements applicable to offshore marine bunkering operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 — principally ss. 13 (incorporation), 14 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), 66 (board powers), 68 (first directors) and 70-83 (governance and fiduciary duties), read with the Companies Regulations, 2011; sectoral overlay: Petroleum Products Act 120 of 1977.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 1.1) submitted with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), directors' consents (Form CoR 1.3), and the reserved name approval; registration evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum authorised or paid-up share capital applies to a (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; no-par-value shares may be issued for nil or nominal consideration, and no escrow account is mandated at incorporation. In practice, the DMRE and TNPA require proof of financial capability and a dedicated operational/storage facility for the bunker licence, assessed separately from share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The issue of 1,000 ordinary no-par-value shares to the subscribers named in the Notice of Incorporation, for the consideration recorded in the Memorandum of Incorporation, be ratified and accepted; 2. The registered office of the Company be established at 12 Harbour Avenue, Cape Town, Western Cape; 3. [Given Name] [Surname] and [Given Name] [Surname] be appointed as directors, each with full powers under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the MOI; 4. [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Company Secretary; 5. The directors be authorised to file the incorporation record with CIPC, open bank accounts, and pursue all bunkering licences required for the business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 9.1 requesting reservation of the name 'ZA (Pty) Ltd' (or a stated trading style), providing up to three alternative names in priority order. Confirm that no identical or confusingly similar registered name or trademark exists. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee electronically and retain the reservation reference, which is valid for 20 business days.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document of the applicant/director
Proof of electronic payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new Form CoR 9.1 with revised alternatives; in similarity disputes, obtain the written consent of the prior name holder or apply to CIPC for an exemption under section 14(3) of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC; company law practitioner or corporate legal adviser
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt either the prescribed standard MOI under the Companies Regulations, 2011 or a custom MOI, ensuring the incorporation record fixes the incorporation date, authorised share classes, directorship rules and governance provisions. Each nominated director must attest Form CoR 1.3 consenting to appointment and confirming no disqualification.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 1.3 director consent of each nominee
Form CoR 1.4 auditor or company secretary consent (where applicable)
Certified copies of directors' identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a compliance query on the MOI, amend the non-compliant clause and re-file; section 14(2) permits company-specific provisions that are not inconsistent with the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Notice of Incorporation and Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form CoR 1.1 together with the final MOI, Form CoR 1.3 consents and the reserved name approval through CIPC e-Services, and pay the incorporation filing fee. CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3), which stands as conclusive evidence of due incorporation; verify the registration number and date of incorporation (normally the filing date).
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate or reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure the defect and resubmit within 10 business days; a refusal may be administratively reviewed under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company for SARS Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete company income tax registration (IT14-style record), register for VAT where taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1 million, register for PAYE and UIF as an employer, and obtain any applicable customs and excise code for fuel movements. SARS issues the income tax reference number and a tax compliance status (TCS) used for licence applications.
required_dossiers: Completed SARS BR01 tax registration application
Certified directors' identity documents and proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to SARS eFiling queries within the stated period and resubmit corrected records; escalated disputes may be directed to a SARS branch office or the Tax Ombud.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) — local Labour Centre; Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first UIF declaration and register the company as an employer with the Compensation Fund under COIDA. Obtain the Compensation Fund Letter of Good Standing, a precondition for petroleum wholesale/bunker licensing and certain port agreements.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office or operational premises address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate delays to the Compensation Fund Commissioner with written representations; challenge any late-payment levy by means of a formal appeal accompanied by proof of filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Accounts and Issue Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution approved by the board; company securities register maintained under CIPC governance rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the board's banking resolution, complete FICA client due diligence forms, and present certified company documents to open the operational account, including any guarantee or escrow facilities required by future bunker counterparties. Concurrently, issue subscriber share certificates and record them in the company's securities register.
required_dossiers: Board resolution approving bank account opening
Certified directors' identity documents and residential address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide enhanced source-of-funds evidence where the bank applies enhanced due diligence; a refusal may be addressed through the Financial Intelligence Centre guidance or the Ombudsman for Banking Services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Mineral Resources and Energy (DMRE) — Petroleum Products Licensing Office; South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA); Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Bunker Supplier / Wholesale Petroleum Products Licence (Registration Certificate under the Petroleum Products Act 120 of 1977 read with the Petroleum Products Regulations, 2022) and TNPA Port Operations Concession for the bunkering berth

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), Environmental Management Inspectorate; provincial authority for the Atmospheric Emission Licence (AEL) under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 (NEM:AQA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment under Listing Notices 1 and 3 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 for bunkering and fuel storage infrastructure; a Full Scoping and EIA Report is prescribed where the listed activity exceeds approximately 500 m³ net petroleum storage or is located adjacent to a sensitive coastal or wetland receptor. AEL under s. 21(1)(g) NEM:AQA applies to the scheduled marine fuel handling process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero oil discharge from bunkering operations per MARPOL Annex I, with oily-water separation to ≤ 15 ppm before any permitted release; National Water Act 36 of 1998 General Authorisations for COD, suspended solids, oil and grease in effluent; AEL fugitive VOC limits to best available techniques (typically ≤ 150 mg/m³ in vent streams); marine fuel sulphur cap of 0.50% m/m per MARPOL 2020; hazardous waste storage and disposal under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local municipal fire service or TNPA port fire services covering the bunkering berth and storage tanks; structural load and tank integrity survey by an accredited registered person under the OHS Act 85 of 1993; occupational health clearance with an approved risk assessment and safe work method statement for bunker delivery; Compensation Fund Letter of Good Standing; ISPS Code Port Facility Security Clearance issued by SAMSA; Dangerous Goods Transport Permit for tanker vehicles serving the site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) (www.sars.gov.za); self-service digital channels: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za) for income tax/VAT/PAYE returns and the SARS Customs Modernisation electronic declaration portal (SAD500) for customs and excise; company incorporation cross-registration with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a South African-incorporated (Pty) Ltd, CIPC integrates incorporation with SARS: the company registration number is issued and an income tax reference number (IT TIN) is auto-created, after which the entity must register for VAT (VAT101 application), PAYE/UIF/SDL, Compensation Fund, and the Customs client code, and it must appoint a resident public officer (s27 Income Tax Act; TAA s246). VAT registration is compulsory when taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period (VAT Act s23), and voluntary registration is available once supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in a 12-month period (s24). A foreign-incorporated enterprise not registered in South Africa must first obtain a SARS tax reference number by physically lodging at a SARS branch or through a registered tax practitioner, submitting certified copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles (or equivalent), board resolution appointing a local public officer/representative taxpayer, a local physical business address, and proof of the South African permanent establishment or enterprise activity (bunkering supply contracts, jetty/tanker charter, or storage licence); SARS will then issue the composite TIN and the applicant may proceed with VAT and customs registrations. All registrations and the taxpayer status pin may be completed on eFiling after initial biometric/TPN onboarding.

Actually, South Africa does not impose a separate branch profits tax; dividends from SA companies to foreign shareholders attract dividend withholding tax at 20%. fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) – Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is freely convertible for current-account trade and service settlements through an Authorised Dealer; the capital account is restricted under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations. Non-resident share capital may be introduced without prior SARB approval if routed through an Authorised Dealer, but every inward investment must be reported and recorded. Profit remittance is available as a current-account outflow once the underlying equity has been issued and the non-resident investor is recorded; the main hurdles are documentary compliance with the bank under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, proof of beneficial ownership, tax-residency certification of the shareholder, and payment/withholding of dividends tax at 15% (reduced under applicable double-taxation agreement only after a treaty relief application has been accepted by SARS). The bank will require board resolutions, solvency confirmation under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and a completed inward/outward investment reporting schedule.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts, including payments for ship bunkering, marine fuel, and lubricant supplies delivered in South African territory to vessels engaged in international trade, must be received in full in South Africa within 180 days from the date of export or rendering of service. FinSurv may extend this period to 365 days in exceptional circumstances upon written application. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into ZAR; exporters may retain foreign currency in an Authorised Dealer-operated Foreign Currency Account (FCA) provided the proceeds are credited through the Authorised Dealer within the 180-day window and the FCA has been applied for in advance. For customs purposes, bunkering supplies are exports under the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964, requiring an EX1 declaration and a Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) to support the surrender of proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low – A foreign digital EMI cannot provide a South African-local clearing account or act as an Authorised Dealer in foreign exchange. It may be used as a supplementary card-issuing or multi-currency collection tool, but it cannot hold ZAR or settle corporate treasury payments without a South African banking counterparty. The Banks Act 94 of 1990 reserves deposit-taking from the public for licensed banks, and an offshore EMI is not licensed by SARB to conduct such business in South Africa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Tier-1 banks require at least one natural-person director or a fully authorised senior officer with a South African connection to attend an in-person KYC interview during account opening. Remote opening is technically possible under FICA where documents are notarised and apostilled, but for a foreign-owned marine bunkering company, banks uniformly require a physical meeting with the managing director or a resident authorised representative. The authorised representative must hold a copy of the board resolution and the signed FICA beneficial ownership register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore shareholders structured through multi-layered fiduciary or bearer share arrangements; bank cannot readily identify ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register (BEN-1), notarised trust deeds, valid passports and source-of-funds statements for all ultimate individuals, 12 months of personal bank statements, and a formal legal opinion confirming the trust's economic and commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure arising from vessel ownership, charterers, or fuel origin from embargoed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results across OFAC, UN, EU, UK HMT and FATF lists; vessel registry certificates and IMO numbers; International Group P&I club confirmation; Bill of Lading and Bunker Delivery Receipts; Marpol certificates; and a compliance undertaking from the marine fuel broker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border transactions not matched by prior shipments or with an unexplained rapid increase in turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA) bunker operator licence; Transnet port terminal agreement; invoice-to-BDN matching; vessel port-call logs; lease agreement for physical office premises; SARS proof of income tax registration and historical audited financials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cash, cryptocurrency, or unlicensed remittance agents for settlement of international bunker purchases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Strict corporate zero-cash policy, bank-certified confirmation that all settlements are via SWIFT MT103 or MT700/MT760 instruments, supplier payment schedules, external audit certificate confirming no cash collections, and compliance with the FATF Recommendation 16 wire transfer rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital contributions for equity must be routed through an Authorised Dealer (Tier-1 commercial bank). The remitting bank sends a SWIFT MT103 with remittance information clearly stating 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION – INWARD INVESTMENT' and the non-resident entity's legal name. The receiving Authorised Dealer requests a board resolution authorising the share issuance, source-of-funds documentation from the investor, and a completed inward investment application; the dealer then allocates the SARB Balance of Payments purpose classification for direct investment equity capital. Funds may be held in the Capital Escrow Account until the share certificate is issued and the non-resident shareholding is endorsed. Once the inward investment is recorded, the escrow balance can be released into the company's operational account for lawful working capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to foreign bunker suppliers, lubricant traders, or port service providers, the South African company must apply to its Authorised Dealer for spot foreign exchange with the underlying commercial contract, invoice, Bunker Delivery Note, and customs documentation. The dealer debits the ZAR operational account, buys the foreign currency, and settles via SWIFT MT103. For larger capital-equipment or significant fuel-import contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) is used; for performance and supply guarantees, a Standby Letter of Credit (MT760) is the customary rail. All outbound payments are reported monthly by the Authorised Dealer to SARB FinSurv, and prepayment for imports is limited to the 90-day threshold unless prior FinSurv approval is obtained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) with a SARB Authorised Dealer, supported by an underlying USD/ZAR payable or receivable arising from physical bunker sales or international fuel purchases; maximum tenor of 12 months.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on USD/ZAR, permitted only where the company has a designated foreign-currency functional currency for the bunkering operation and the transaction is executed through a SARB-registered dealer with FinSurv notification; otherwise, NDFs are reserved for non-resident shareholders.

Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) with an Authorised Dealer for hedging a long-term US dollar-denominated term loan provided by the non-resident parent, subject to FinSurv approval of the underlying foreign-loan facility and full documentation of interest and principal flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) - statutory declaration of company name, registered office, directors, principal business and Public Interest Score (PIS); fee assumes PIS 500+ top tier for a trading bunkering entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the incorporation date; e-filed via CIPC Annual Return portal; no calendar-year-end rule applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty accrues at 10% of the annual return fee per month or part thereof; company flagged 'in default' and a compliance notice is issued; failure to file for more than two annual return periods triggers strike-off under s82(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Strike-off is gazetted; reinstatement costs approximately R1,000 (USD 53) plus all outstanding annual return fees, and directors trading during deregistration incur joint and several personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (BO) Schedule - annual confirmation and event-driven e-filing for every share issue, transfer or change in qualifying beneficial interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership e-filing module (Companies Act s50-51 as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual BO confirmation filed concurrently with the annual return on the incorporation anniversary; any share transfer or UBO change filed within 30 calendar days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: BO schedule is a mandatory component of the annual return; default prevents CIPC from processing the annual return and exposes the company and each director to a compliance notice, an administrative fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 (USD 53,500) per contravention, or, on conviction, a fine and/or imprisonment for up to 10 years under s216; persistent default accelerates the s82 strike-off track.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) - preparation, independent statutory audit and board approval (no standing CIPC lodgment for a private company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with CIPC for a (Pty) Ltd; retained at the registered office and produced within the period stipulated in a CIPC request under s33(2)(b)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS and the auditor's report must be completed within 6 months after financial year-end and approved by the board (e.g., FYE 31 Dec requires board approval by 30 Jun); the audit report accompanies the AFS under s33(1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to produce AFS on CIPC demand triggers a s33(7) compliance notice and an administrative fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 (USD 53,500); directors may be held jointly and severally liable for losses caused by the default, and the company is treated as delinquent for annual return purposes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (effective for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; prior years 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday. Standard 27% rate applies to bunkering and refueling profits. Deductions include s.11(o) IP amortisation, s.12C manufacturing or similar capital allowances, s.12D and s.12Q environmental and energy efficiency allowances, and s.11D research and development incentives. The effective rate remains 27% absent qualifying expenditure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Corporate Income Tax Return; filed electronically via SARS eFiling portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 12 months of the company's financial year-end; provisional tax returns (IRP6) are due at the 6-month interim and at the year-end, with a third 'top-up' payment within 7 months of year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total turnover or gross receipts from ship bunkering, marine fuel and lubricant sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only South African-sourced turnover attributable to a South African permanent establishment or branch; foreign source income may be taxable if connected to the SA business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including bunker fuel and lubricant acquisition costs, vessel expenses and operational services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use actual invoiced costs, applying arm's length principle under s.31 for connected-party purchases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit after cost of sales adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same computation as for local companies; gross profit must be determined in accordance with SA tax standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits (s.6quat) for foreign taxes paid on income included within the South African tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only where foreign taxes are proven and the associated income is actually taxable in South Africa under the applicable double tax agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, including dividends, and other non-taxable receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude income exempt under the Income Tax Act or under a DTA; shipping and international transport income may attract separate treaty treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenditure and allowances, including repairs, crew costs, lease or depot overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenditure incurred for the production of South African taxable income is deductible; head-office overheads require fair allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss balance brought forward and current year assessed loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restrict claimed assessed losses to losses sustained in respect of the SA permanent establishment; this schema applies a 5-year exposure limit; confirm current-year constellation with SARS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before further assessed loss set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed from SA source; an SA permanent establishment cannot apply losses of the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal company tax at 27% before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 27% rate on Box 31; offset provisional tax credits and foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes and additional taxes, including dividends tax and capital gains tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare distributions to non-residents and compute 20% dividends tax or lower treaty rate as applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of ITR14 triggers administrative penalties under s.210-211 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011: a percentage-based penalty of 10% of the assessed tax on first default and up to 20% on repeat default, plus interest at 10.5% per annum on any unpaid tax amount. SARS may issue ex parte assessments and fixed monthly penalties for large taxpayers, potentially exceeding ZAR 16,500 per month until compliance is achieved.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced or nil dividend withholding tax rate under a double tax agreement, the non-resident beneficiary must submit a formal declaration and Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the South African paying company or authorised financial institution before distribution. SARS requires the completion of a DTA declaration form (previously NWD.01 or similar), and where a directive is required, a reduced-rate directive must be requested via SARS eFiling. The payer must retain documentary evidence; refund of excess withholding is obtainable through SARS if the directive is issued after the dividend payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalty withholding tax: statutory rate 15%, treaty-reduced rates commonly 0%-10%. Interest withholding tax: statutory rate 15%, with statutory exemptions for listed debt and interest paid to non-residents under specific instruments; DTA- reduced rates commonly 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 5,000,000 aggregate annual cross-border connected-party transactions (South Africa does not impose a fixed statutory threshold; SARS may require transfer pricing documentation, including Master File and Local File, where the aggregate value of affected transactions exceeds ZAR 5 million or on a risk-based audit selection).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have a separate 'Economic Substance Regulations' regime comparable to UAE or Cayman. However, the doctrine is applied through the Income Tax Act's s.80A-GAAR, s.31 transfer pricing rules, the 'place of effective management' residence test, and controlled foreign company (CFC) legislation. SARS will disregard or re-characterise a transaction or corporate form where commercial substance is absent. For bunkering entities, the presence of local operational control, management decisions and tanker/bunker supply capacity is essential.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing or misclassifying bunker fuel sales volumes, using fabricated purchase invoices to inflate cost of sales, or failing to register for corporate income tax despite carrying on a business in South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS ex parte assessment; understatement penalty of up to 200% of the resultant shortfall under s.222 of the Tax Administration Act; criminal prosecution under s.235 TAA: fine up to ZAR 2,000,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally responsible under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (s.77(9)) for unlawful distributions or reckless trading; SARS may pierce the corporate veil where the Pty Ltd is used as a facade; travel bans and restriction orders are possible under s.183 TAA; imprisonment is a personal criminal consequence for directors who knowingly participated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SA company with no employees, premises or decision-making power, used exclusively as an invoice intermediary between foreign bunker suppliers and vessels, with profits artificially shifted to tax haven entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS re-characterisation of transactions, disallowing excessive deductions, invoking GAAR adjustments (s.80A-L), and applying transfer pricing penalties. Understatement penalties of 50%-200% may apply; the company's registration may be deregistered by CIPC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal assessment where the corporate veil is pierced; liability for unpaid tax arises under common law and s.169(1)(b) of the Income Tax Act; disqualification from holding directorships and travel bans may be imposed; criminal prosecution for reckless trading under the Companies Act may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade-Based Money Laundering and Sanctions Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing bunker payments in cash or convertible instruments, failing to verify beneficial owners of counterparties, disguising sanctioned vessel flag-state transfers or concealing STS (ship-to-ship) cargo transfers on prohibited routes, or failing to file STRs with the FIC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial Intelligence Centre Act administrative penalties up to ZAR 10 million per violation; Customs and Excise Act penalties for false declarations: fine of up to 10 times the value of the goods and twice the duty evaded, plus imprisonment of up to 5 years; criminal asset forfeiture under POCA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently facilitate trade-based money laundering or sanctions violations are personally exposed to civil damages, joint and several penalty liability, asset forfeiture orders, travel bans, loss of professional licences, and imprisonment for up to 15 years under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act and the Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act.
